Q: What is MSA University and where is it located?
A: October University for Modern Sciences and Arts (MSA University) is a leading private university located in 6th of October City, Giza, Egypt, at the intersection of the 26th of July Mehwar Road and Wahat Road, about 30 km from central Cairo. The official hotline is 16672 (international landline 002 0216672), support email is info@msa.edu.eg, and the website is msa.edu.eg.
chunks.heading: MSA University Overview and Location

chunks.text: Q: Which British universities partner with MSA University for dual degrees? A: MSA University operates a dual degree system where graduates earn both an Egyptian bachelor degree accredited by the Supreme Council of Universities and a British bachelor degree validated by either the University of Greenwich or the University of Bedfordshire, enabling direct postgraduate study in the UK without traditional degree equivalence. Q: Which MSA faculties are partnered with the University of Greenwich? A: Six faculties partner with the University of Greenwich: Faculty of Engineering, Faculty of Pharmacy, Faculty of Computer Sciences, Faculty of Biotechnology, Faculty of Management Sciences, and Faculty of Nutrition and Food Technology.
chunks.heading: Dual British Degree Partnerships

chunks.text: of Biotechnology, Faculty of Management Sciences, and Faculty of Nutrition and Food Technology. Q: Which MSA faculties are partnered with the University of Bedfordshire? A: Four faculties partner with the University of Bedfordshire: Faculty of Mass Communication, Faculty of Languages, Faculty of Arts and Design, and Faculty of Physical Therapy. The Faculty of Oral and Dental Medicine operates under the main Egyptian accreditation system within MSA University.
chunks.heading: Dual British Degree Partnerships

chunks.text:
Q: Does MSA University provide campus buses and where do I subscribe?
A: Yes. MSA University operates a private bus fleet covering Greater Cairo and Giza including 6th of October, Sheikh Zayed, Palm Hills, Dream Park, Al Motamayez, Hadayek El Ahram, Haram, Faisal, Mohandessin, Maadi, Mokattam, Nasr City, Heliopolis, Shubra, New Cairo, Al Rehab, Madinaty, and Helwan. Students manage bus subscriptions at the official Bus Room in Room K108.
chunks.heading: University Transportation and Bus Services

chunks.text:
Q: What is the attendance rule and absence limit at MSA University?
A: Students at MSA University must maintain a minimum attendance rate of 75 percent across all lectures, tutorials, and laboratories for each module. Falling below 75 percent attendance (even with medical or emergency absences) leads to deprivation from the final exam and automatic failure in that module. For regular classes, late entry is permitted only during the first 5 minutes; after 5 minutes the student is marked absent.
chunks.heading: MSA University Attendance and Class Arrival Rules

chunks.text: Q: What are the late arrival rules for midterm and final exams at MSA University? A: For 1.5 hour midterm exams, students are allowed entry only within the first 15 minutes. For 3 hour final exams, entry is permitted up to the first 30 minutes. Students must bring their official MSA University Student ID card to attend examinations and enter campus facilities. Q: What are the plagiarism and academic misconduct rules at MSA University? A: MSA University enforces strict academic integrity rules. Plagiarism includes quoting words or paragraphs without proper citation, paraphrasing someone else's ideas without acknowledgment, borrowing unacknowledged data, or copying another student's assignments, computer code, or exam answers.
chunks.heading: Exam Entry Rules and Academic Integrity

chunks.text: g unacknowledged data, or copying another student's assignments, computer code, or exam answers. Suspected violations trigger a formal faculty investigation committee.
chunks.heading: Exam Entry Rules and Academic Integrity

chunks.text:
Q: How do credit hours, GPA, and academic probation work at MSA University?
A: MSA University follows a 4.0 letter grading scale (A through D, Fail = 0). Bachelor programs typically require at least 140 credit hours across four academic years (8 semesters), depending on the faculty. In the summer semester, students may register for a maximum of 7 credit hours. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 is required for good academic standing and graduation. Students whose cumulative GPA falls below 2.0 are placed on academic probation with restricted course load until their cumulative GPA returns to 2.0 or higher. When repeating a module, only the highest earned grade counts toward the cumulative GPA.
chunks.heading: Credit Hours, GPA Scale, and Academic Probation

chunks.text:
Q: What is required for course registration and the English Language Placement Test (ELPT) at MSA University?
A: Before registering courses during the academic calendar advising period, students must register their bank tuition payment receipts with the MSA Accounting Department. All new applicants must take the English Language Placement Test (ELPT) unless exempt with valid IELTS, TOEFL, IGCSE English grade B or 6+, IB, Canadian diploma, or qualifying SAT, ACT, or EST scores. The online ELPT can be taken one time only; any retake or reset must be taken physically on campus.
chunks.heading: Registration, Financial Clearance, and English Placement Test (ELPT)

chunks.text: Q: What general documents are required for admission to MSA University? A: All new applicants submit 5 recent passport photos, 2 original computerized Egyptian birth certificates (or authenticated birth certificates for non Egyptians), copies of student and parent National ID cards, passport copy if available, and for Egyptian male students military service Form 2 Gond plus Form 6 or 7 Gond. Q: What are the certificate requirements for Thanaweya Amma, IGCSE, and American Diploma at MSA University? A: Thanaweya Amma students submit their original stamped certificate matching the required faculty section (Scientific Math for Engineering; Scientific Science for Pharmacy, Dentistry, and Physical Therapy).
chunks.heading: Admission Requirements and Required Documents at MSA University

chunks.text: entific Math for Engineering; Scientific Science for Pharmacy, Dentistry, and Physical Therapy). IGCSE students submit original certificates authenticated by the British Council, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Ministry of Education, proof of 12 years of schooling, and stamped Arabic, Religion, and Civics certificates, with 8 subjects (up to 9 for some faculties), minimum grade C (OL) or D (AL/ASL), within 4 successive years. American Diploma students submit an authenticated official transcript with 8 to 9 subjects (at least 4 from Grade 12, max 2 from Grade 10, minimum 1 credit each), SAT 1 or EST 1 score of at least 800 (or ACT 1 score of 14), and SAT 2, EST 2, or ACT 2 score of at least 900 for faculties requiring subject tests.

Q: What is the architectural design and campus layout of MSA University in 6th of October?
A: MSA University occupies a 50 acre permanent campus in 6th of October City designed around open green landscapes, pedestrian courtyards, natural ventilation, and eco friendly sustainable architecture. Campus architectural highlights include the MSA Center of Earth constructed with Compressed Stabilized Earth Blocks (CSEB), the landmark 1,150 seat Opera House in Building G, the El Degwi Mosque, 31 cafeterias and food courts, and comprehensive sports grounds including football, basketball, volleyball, padel courts, and the MSA Gym.
chunks.heading: MSA University Campus Layout and Architectural Design

chunks.text: Q: What is located in Building 1, Building 2 (SSB), and Building 3 at MSA University? A: Building 1 houses University Administration, the Faculty of Languages, the Faculty of Mass Communication, and the Faculty of Management Sciences. Building 2 is the Student Services Building (SSB), serving as the central hub for student affairs, student activities, career events like Build Your Future, seminar spaces, and the renovated campus Cinema Hall. Building 3 houses the major scientific and technical faculties: Faculty of Pharmacy, Faculty of Engineering, Faculty of Biotechnology, Faculty of Computer Science, and Faculty of Dentistry. Q: What does the Architecture Department at MSA University study and what facilities does it have?
A: The Faculty of Engineering offers a Bachelor degree in Architectural Systems Engineering (ASE) validated with the University of Greenwich. Its studio based curriculum covers Architectural Design, History and Theories of Architecture, Urban Planning, Landscape Design, Interior Design, Environmental Control Systems, Computer Graphics, and Construction Management. Students work in dedicated architectural design studios, digital computer labs, engineering workshops in Building 6, and sustainable architecture spaces such as the MSA Center of Earth.

Q: How do room numbers and building letters work at MSA University?
A: MSA University room codes combine a building letter and a three digit number where the first digit indicates the floor and the last two digits indicate the room number: 1xx is the First floor at ground level (no stairs or elevator needed), 2xx is the Second floor upstairs, 3xx is the Third floor, and 4xx is the Fourth floor. For example, Room C111 is in Building C on the ground level First floor (Room 11), and Room G204 is in Building G on the Second floor (Room 04).

A: Upon graduation from MSA University, students receive two accredited bachelor degrees: one approved by the Egyptian Ministry of Higher Education and Supreme Council of Universities, and a second validated by a UK partner university (University of Greenwich for Engineering, Computer Science, Pharmacy, Biotechnology, Management Sciences, and Nutrition; University of Bedfordshire for Mass Communication, Languages, Arts and Design, and Physical Therapy). Graduates can pursue postgraduate studies in the UK and internationally without traditional degree equivalency procedures. In addition to regular tuition, students pay a British validation fee during the first semester of each academic year in British Pounds or its USD equivalent. chunks.text: س: كيف تعمل الشهادة البريطانية المزدوجة في MSA وهل تحتاج معادلة في بريطانيا؟ ج: يحصل خريج جامعة MSA على شهادتي بكالوريوس معتمدتين: شهادة معتمدة من وزارة التعليم العالي والمجلس الأعلى للجامعات المصري، وشهادة بريطانية معتمدة من جامعة جرينتش (لكليات الهندسة، علوم الحاسب، الصيدلة، التكنولوجيا الحيوية، العلوم الإدارية، والتغذية) أو جامعة بيدفوردشير (لكليات الإعلام، اللغات، الفنون والتصميم، والعلاج الطبيعي)، مما يتيح استكمال الدراسات العليا في بريطانيا بدون الحاجة لإجراءات المعادلة التقليدية. س: هل خريجو جامعة MSA مؤهلون للانضمام للنقابات المهنية المصرية؟ ج: نعم.
chunks.heading: أكثر 5 أسئلة شائعة عن جامعة MSA على الإنترنت

chunks.text: اءات المعادلة التقليدية. س: هل خريجو جامعة MSA مؤهلون للانضمام للنقابات المهنية المصرية؟ ج: نعم. نظراً لأن جميع درجات جامعة MSA معتمدة رسمياً من وزارة التعليم العالي والمجلس الأعلى للجامعات المصري، فإن الخريجين مؤهلون للانضمام لنقاباتهم المهنية الرسمية مثل نقابة المهندسين، نقابة الصيادلة، نقابة أطباء الأسنان، نقابة العلاج الطبيعي، نقابة الصحفيين، ونقابة التشكيليين. س: كيف تُدفع المصروفات الدراسية ورسوم الاعتماد البريطاني والزيادة السنوية في MSA؟ ج: يسدد الطلاب المصريون المصروفات الدراسية بالجنيه المصري داخل الحرم الجامعي، بينما يسدد الطلاب غير المصريين بالدولار الأمريكي عبر فرع البنك الأهلي المصري بالحرم الجامعي.
chunks.heading: أكثر 5 أسئلة شائعة عن جامعة MSA على الإنترنت

chunks.text: عي، بينما يسدد الطلاب غير المصريين بالدولار الأمريكي عبر فرع البنك الأهلي المصري بالحرم الجامعي. كما تُدفع رسوم الاعتماد البريطاني في الفصل الدراسي الأول من كل عام بالجنيه الإسترليني أو ما يعادله بالدولار، وتخضع المصروفات لزيادة سنوية تتراوح عادةً بين 10% و15%. س: ما هي المنح الدراسية والخصومات المتاحة في جامعة MSA؟ ج: توفر جامعة MSA عدة منح وخصومات: منحة تصل إلى 100% لأوائل الثانوية العامة على مستوى الجمهورية، خصم تفوق أكاديمي بين 10% و20% حسب المعدل التراكمي، خصم حوالي 5% للتقديم المبكر أو السداد السنوي الكامل، خصم 15% لأبناء خريجي نفس الكلية، خصم 20% لأعضاء الأندية المتعاقدة (مثل الجزيرة ونيو جيزة وبالم هيلز)، ومنح رياضية من 10% حتى 75% لأبطال المنتخبات الوطنية. س: هل يمكن السفر في برنامج الدراسة الصيفي ببريطانيا أو التحويل من جامعة أخرى إلى MSA؟ ج: نعم.

chunks.text: ة. س: هل يمكن السفر في برنامج الدراسة الصيفي ببريطانيا أو التحويل من جامعة أخرى إلى MSA؟ ج: نعم. تنظم جامعة MSA منذ أكثر من 22 عاماً برنامج الدراسة الصيفي في بريطانيا (UK Summer Abroad Programme) بالتعاون مع جامعتي جرينتش وبيدفوردشير للطلاب المتميزين أكاديمياً لدراسة مسارات متخصصة مثل الذكاء الاصطناعي وعلوم البيانات والإعلام، كما تقبل الجامعة التحويل من الجامعات المعتمدة وفق ضوابط المجلس الأعلى للجامعات ومقاصة الساعات المعتمدة.

chunks.text: س: فين موقع جامعة MSA وإيه رقم الخط الساخن والتواصل؟ ج: تقع جامعة أكتوبر للعلوم الحديثة والآداب (MSA) في مدينة السادس من أكتوبر بمحافظة الجيزة عند تقاطع محور 26 يوليو مع طريق الواحات على بُعد 30 كم من وسط القاهرة. الخط الساخن الرسمي هو 16672، البريد الإلكتروني info@msa.edu.eg، والموقع الرسمي msa.edu.eg. س: ما هي الكليات والشراكات البريطانية في جامعة MSA؟ ج: تمنح جامعة MSA شهادة مزدوجة معتمدة من المجلس الأعلى للجامعات المصري ومن جامعة بريطانية شريكة بدون الحاجة لمعادلة للدراسات العليا في بريطانيا. الكليات الشريكة مع جامعة جرينتش (University of Greenwich) هي: الهندسة، الصيدلة، علوم الحاسب، التكنولوجيا الحيوية، العلوم الإدارية، والتغذية وتكنولوجيا الغذاء.

chunks.text: س: ما هي التصميمات المعمارية ومساحة حرم جامعة MSA؟ ج: يمتد الحرم الجامعي لجامعة MSA على مساحة 50 فداناً في مدينة 6 أكتوبر بتصميم معماري حديث يعتمد على المساحات الخضراء المفتوحة والتهوية الطبيعية والعمارة المستدامة، ويضم مركز الأرض المستدام (MSA Center of Earth) المبني ببلوكات التربة المضغوطة المستقرة (CSEB)، ومسجد الدجوي، و31 كافتيريا ومنطقة مطاعم (Food Courts)، وملاعب كرة قدم وسلة وطائرة وبادل، وجيم الجامعة. س: ما هو دليل مباني جامعة MSA (مبنى 1 حتى 13 ومبنى SSB ومبنى G)؟ ج: مبنى 1 يضم الإدارة وكلية اللغات والإعلام والعلوم الإدارية. مبنى 2 هو مبنى خدمات الطلاب (SSB) ويضم شؤون الطلاب والأنشطة وقاعة السينما الجامعية وفعاليات التوظيف. مبنى 3 يضم كليات الصيدلة والهندسة والتكنولوجيا الحيوية وعلوم الحاسب وطب الأسنان.

chunks.text: س: ما هي قواعد الحضور والغياب ودخول المحاضرات والامتحانات في جامعة MSA؟ ج: يشترط حضور 75% على الأقل في المحاضرات والسكاشن والمعامل لكل مادة، وتجاوز نسبة الغياب 25% يؤدي إلى الحرمان من دخول الامتحان النهائي والرسوب في المادة. يُسمح بدخول المحاضرة خلال أول 5 دقائق فقط وبعدها يُسجل الطالب غائباً. وفي الامتحانات يُسمح بالتأخير بحد أقصى 15 دقيقة في الميدتيرم و30 دقيقة في الامتحان النهائي مع ضرورة إحضار كارنيه الجامعة (Student ID). س: ما هي قواعد الساعات المعتمدة والمعدل التراكمي والإنذار الأكاديمي (Probation) والانتحال؟ ج: يعمل النظام بنظام الساعات المعتمدة ومعدل تراكمي من 4.0 (عادةً لا يقل عن 140 ساعة معتمدة خلال 4 سنوات حسب الكلية)، والحد الأقصى للفصل الصيفي هو 7 ساعات معتمدة.

chunks.text: لا يقل عن 140 ساعة معتمدة خلال 4 سنوات حسب الكلية)، والحد الأقصى للفصل الصيفي هو 7 ساعات معتمدة. الحد الأدنى للمعدل التراكمي للتخرج والاستمرار بدون إنذار هو 2.0، وإذا قل المعدل عن 2.0 يدخل الطالب في الإنذار الأكاديمي (Probation) بعبء دراسي مخفض، وعند إعادة مادة يُحتسب أعلى تقدير فقط. كما تطبق الجامعة لوائح صارمة ضد الانتحال العلمي والغش (Plagiarism) ويُشترط تسجيل إيصال المصروفات بإدارة الحسابات قبل تسجيل المواد.

س: إيه الأوراق المطلوبة للتقديم في جامعة MSA واختبار تحديد مستوى الإنجليزية (ELPT)؟
ج: الأوراق العامة المطلوبة هي 5 صور شخصية حديثة، أصل شهادة الميلاد المميكنة (نسختان)، صورة بطاقة الطالب وولي الأمر، صورة جواز السفر إن وجد، وللطلاب الذكور المصريين نموذج 2 جند ونموذج 6 أو 7 جند، بالإضافة إلى أصل شهادة الثانوية العامة أو شهادات IGCSE الموثقة (8 مواد بحد أدنى C للـ OL و D للـ AL مع إثبات 12 سنة دراسة) أو الدبلومة الأمريكية الموثقة (8 إلى 9 مواد مع حد أدنى 800 في SAT 1 أو EST 1 و900 في SAT 2 أو EST 2 للكليات العلمية). كما يشترط اجتياز اختبار اللغة الإنجليزية (ELPT) أونلاين مرة واحدة فقط أو داخل الحرم الجامعي ما لم يكن الطالب معفى بشهادة IELTS أو TOEFL أو ما يعادلها.

Project Title:
Edge AI Avatar for Campus Assistant for New Student Onboarding
An Offline LLM-Powered Voice Interactive System

Project Overview:
This project proposes the development of an intelligent, offline, Edge AI-powered
campus assistant designed to welcome and guide the first batch of new students.
The system acts as a virtual receptionist that can understand student inquiries in
both voice and text (Arabic & English) and provide instant, accurate responses
about admission, departments, schedules, campus facilities, and academic
regulations without requiring an internet connection. Unlike traditional cloud-
based chatbots, this system performs all AI inference locally on the edge device
(Raspberry Pi 3/4/5), ensuring data privacy, zero latency, and 24/7 availability
even with poor internet connectivity.
chunks.heading: Project Title:
chunks.source_file: GA P2 Offline AI AvatarCampus Assistant.pdf

chunks.text:
Problem Statement:
New students in the first batch face significant challenges due to lack of
information, absence of senior students to guide them, and overload on
administrative staff. They repeatedly ask about: Where is my lecture hall? What
are the required documents? What is the difference between departments? There is a need for an intelligent, always-available assistant that understands
natural language, not just fixed buttons. Objectives:
 To design an offline AI assistant using Large Language Model (LLM), that is
optimized and running on edge hardware.  To implement a multimodal interface: Voice-to-Text and Text-to-Voice
interaction.  To provide accurate, context-aware answers about the faculty and
university using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).  To deploy the system on a standalone low-cost, low-power edge device.
chunks.heading: Problem Statement:
chunks.source_file: GA P2 Offline AI AvatarCampus Assistant.pdf

chunks.text:

Hardware Layer:
Main Brain: Raspberry Pi 3/4/5 (...GB RAM) as Edge Server Sensors: USB
Microphone + Speaker + Touch Display (7-inch) Microcontroller Nodes (Optional):
ESP32-S3 modules for distributed info kiosks around campus connected via
MQTTB. Software Layer (Full Edge AI Stack):
Speech-to-Text (STT): Whisper.cpp (tiny/base model), converts student voice query to
text locally. Brain (LLM): Phi-3 Mini (3.8B) / Llama 3.2 1B quantized to 4-bit (Q4_K_M) running
via Ollama / llama.cpp on Raspberry Pi. No cloud API. Knowledge Base (RAG): All faculty FAQs,
bylaws, and maps are converted to embeddings using nomic-embed-text and stored in a local
vector database (ChromaDB). This prevents hallucination.

Acting Humanly?
A Turing Test is a method of inquiry in AI to determine whether or not a
computer is capable of acting like a human. The Turing test, originally called
the imitation game by Alan Turing in 1950, is a test of a machine's ability to
exhibit intelligent behaviour equivalent to, or indistinguishable from, that of a
human.
It Involves an interpreter (C), a human (B), and a AI-based computer (A).
The computer (A) and human (B) have separate conversations with the interpreter (C).
If the interpreter can’t differentiate between the computer && human, then the
computer has a form of AI.

Narrow AI: It has a narrow scope in terms of what it can do  (Can do one task
really well). Not generalized. The idea behind weak AI isn’t to mimic human
intelligence. Rather, it’s to simulate human behaviour.

limited pre-defined range of functions. They are in particular not examples of strong AI
as there are neither genuine intelligence nor self-awareness.

Intelligent Agents
How a software agent is different from traditional software?  Agents have social ability, that is, they communicate with the user, system,
and other agents as required.  Agents may also co-operate with other agents to carry out more complex
tasks than they themselves can handle.  Agents may migrate from one system to another to access remote resources
or even to meet other agents (Mobile Agents).  Agents contain some level of intelligence, from fixed rules to learning
engines that allow them to adapt to changes in the environment.  Agents don't only act reactively, but sometimes can act proactively
Traditional Software: Follows pre-defined, static paths of logic (Condition-Action rules). It's
a deterministic mapping of input to output. Software Agent: Uses dynamic reasoning and planning to achieve a goal.

chunks.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Agentic AI
AI systems that transcend passive response and instead, exhibit goal-directed
autonomous behavior. Unlike traditional AI that perform a single, specific task upon
prompt (Generate report), an agentic AI is given a high-level objective and independently
plans, executes, adapts a sequence of actions to achieve it.
Agentic AI represents the next
evolutionary step, moving from
reactive  proactive, executive
intelligence, where AI becomes a
general-purpose problem-solver
capable of managing complex,
multi-step workflows.
Traditional AI (ChatGPT): Functions as a tool. A user must provide precise prompts and manage
the entire workflow. Agentic AI: Functions as an autonomous actor in which the user provides

Agents choose actions based on a preference (utility) for each state. Goals

When there are multiple possible alternatives, how to decide which one is best?
Goals are qualitative: A goal specifies a crude distinction between a happy and
unhappy state, but often need a more general performance measure that describes
“degree of happiness.”
Utility function U: State  R indicating a measure of success / happiness of agent

of being achieved and you need to weigh the likelihood of success against the
importance of a goal.

Activation functions are functions used in a NN to compute the weighted sum of

or non-linear function of input n. Activation functions add non-linearity to the output
which enables NN to solve non-linear problems.
AS an example, the hard-limit activation function sets the output of the neuron to 0 if
the function argument (n) is less than 0, or 1 if its argument is greater than or equal to 0.

Un-informed Search
Un-informed search is a class of search algorithms which operates
in brute force-way. They do not have additional information about
state or search space, so called blind search. Following are the
various types of un-informed search algorithms:
Breadth-first Search
Depth-first Search
Uniform cost search
Comparing BFS and DFS, the big advantage of DFS is that it has
much lower memory requirements, because it’s not necessary to
store all of the child pointers at each level. Depending on the data
and what you are looking for, either DFS or BFS could be
advantageous.
chunks.heading: Search Techniques

chunks.text:
Search Techniques
Un-informed Search
Breadth-first search is the most common search strategy for traversing a
tree/graph. This algorithm searches breadth-wise, so it is called breadth-first
search. BFS algorithm starts searching from the root node of the tree and
expands all successor nodes at the current level before moving to nodes of
next level. BFS implemented using FIFO queue data structure.
Advantages:
BFS will provide a solution if any one exists (completeness).
If there are more than one solutions, then BFS will provide the minimal
solution which requires the least number of steps.
Disadvantages:
It requires lots of memory since each level of the tree must be saved into
memory to expand the next level.
BFS needs lots of time if the solution is far away from the root node.
Breadth-first Search
chunks.heading: Search Techniques

chunks.text:
Search Techniques
Un-informed Search
Depth-first search is a recursive algorithm for traversing a tree/graph. It is
called the depth-first search because it starts from the root node and follows
each path to its greatest depth node before moving to the next path. DFS
uses a stack data structure. The process of DFS algorithm is similar to BFS.
Advantage:
DFS requires very less memory as it only needs to store a stack of the nodes on
the path from root node to the current node.
It takes less time to reach to the goal node than BFS algorithm (if it traverses in
the right path).
Disadvantage:
It is possible that many states keep re-occurring, and there is no guarantee of
finding the solution.
DFS algorithm goes for deep down searching and sometime it may go to the
infinite loop.
Depth-first Search

Compare between BFS and DFS Search techniques
Advantages of DFS
Memory-efficient – less memory than BFS. Only path from root to current node is needed. Time Efficient. Disadvantages of DFS
Does not guaranteed to find the solution if it exists. Stuck in loops. Non-optimal solution. Stuck in Local minimum. Advantages of BFS
Optimal Solution – BFS is guaranteed to find the shortest path between two nodes. Completeness – BFS is complete, meaning it will find the solution if it exists. Level-wise traversal – BFS visits all the nodes at a given level before moving to the next
level. This approach makes it useful in certain scenarios such as finding the shortest path or
exploring a game state. Disadvantages of BFS
Space complexity – BFS is memory-intensive, especially for large graphs or trees.

K-Means Clustering Algorithm
The main goal of K-Means is to find groups in data and the number of groups is
represented by K. It is an iterative procedure where each data point is assigned
to one of the K groups based on feature similarity.
An iterative clustering algorithm
– Initialize: Pick K random points as cluster centers
– Iterate:
1. Assign data points to closest cluster center
2. Update the cluster center to the average of its assigned points
– Repeat until no points assignments change
Goal: Minimize Intra-
cluster inertia

K-Means Clustering
The k-means clustering algorithm aims to
choose cluster centers, that minimize inertia.
Inertia is calculated by measuring the distance
between a datapoint and its centroid, squaring the
distance and summing those squares for each data
point in the cluster. The sum is the intra-cluster
distance.
The lower the sum the better because it means that
the datapoints within the cluster are compact or more
similar.
Inertia, an evaluation metric that measures how well a
dataset has been clustered based on chosen distance metrics.

chunks.text:
K-Means Initialization Sensitivity
Why Local Minima Persist?
Greedy Assignment: Points are assigned to the nearest centroid
right now, does not consider the centroids future movements.
Lock-in Effect: Once assignments are made, centroids can only
move within their assigned points, creating a self-reinforcing trap.
No Global View: The algorithm never considers whether moving a
centroid would allow data assignments that lead to lower overall-
inertia.
Convex but Constrained: Each individual update step is optimal,
but the combination leads to local optima at the end.

What is the goal of an agent in reinforcement learning?
To maximize its total cumulative reward over time.
What is a state in reinforcement learning?
A representation of the current situation of the environment.
What is an action in reinforcement learning?
A decision / move made by the agent to interact with the environment.
What is a reward in reinforcement learning?
A feedback signal from the environment that quantifies the benefit of taking a
particular action in a particular state.
What is a policy in reinforcement learning?
A strategy (mapping from states to actions) that defines the agent's behavior in the
environment.
What is the difference between exploration and exploitation in
reinforcement learning?
Exploration is trying new actions to discover their effects, while exploitation is choosing
the best-known action to maximize rewards.

chunks.text:
What is the Q-value in Q-learning? The expected cumulative reward of taking particular action in a particular state and
following a particular policy. What does the Q in Q-learning stand for? It represents the quality (value) of taking a particular action in a particular state. Is Q-learning a model-free or model-based approach? Model-free. How does Q-learning handle exploration and exploitation? Typically, by using an ε-greedy strategy, where the agent explores with probability ε
and exploits with probability 1-ε. So, the ϵ-greedy strategy is used to balance
exploration and exploitation during the action selection phase, and the Q-learning
update equation is used to update the Q-values based on the experiences of the
agent. Action Selection (Using ϵ-Greedy Strategy):
With probability ε, choose a random action (exploration).

Microprocessor is a controlling unit of a micro-computer, fabricated on a small chip
capable of performing arithmetic and logical operations as well as communicating
with the other devices (Digital System).
Block Diagram of a Basic Micro-computer
Initially, the instructions are stored in the memory in a sequential order. The
microprocessor fetches such instructions from the memory, then decodes them and
executes those instructions till STOP/HLT instruction is reached. Later, it sends the
result in binary to the output port/M-Location. Between these processes, registers store
the data temporarily in which ALU performs the computing functions.

3.1- Arithmetic and logical unit (ALU):
It is multi-operational combinational logic circuit. It performs arithmetic and
logical operations.
1. It is always controlled by timing and control circuits.
2. It is 8-bit.
3. It provides status to the flag register.
-Adder: It performs arithmetic operations  accumulator.
-Shifter: It performs logical operations. Result of operation  accumulator.
-Status Register: Reflects the status of ALU or controls certain operations.

3.4-Flag Register:
Flag register is a group of flip flops used to give the status of operation result.
The flag register is connected to ALU.
Once an operation is performed by ALU, the result is transferred on internal data
bus && status of result will be stored in flags.
They are Zero (Z), Carry (CY), Sign (S), Parity (P), and Auxiliary Carry (AC)
flags.
3.2-Accumulator (Accessible):
It is 8-bit general purpose register of microprocessor called as A register.
The result of an operation is stored in the accumulator by default.
3.3-Temporary Register (Not Accessible):
8-bit can provides operands to ALU.

3.5. A General purpose registers (GPRs):
Apart from accumulator, 8085 consists of B, C, D, E, H and L. Each one can hold
data of size 8-bit.
These registers can also be used to work in pairs to hold 16-bit data such as B-C,
D-E and H-L to store 16-bit data.
The H-L pair works as a memory pointer that holds the address of a particular
memory location and can store 16-bit address as they work in pair.
3.5. B Special purpose register (SPRs):
Program counter (PC) holds the address of the next instruction to be executed from
memory. PC is a 16-bit register.
Stack pointer (SP): is also a 16-bit register which is used as a memory pointer (Top
of the stack).

These buffers are used to drive the external address bus and address-data bus. As the memory-I/O chips are connected to these buses, the CPU can exchange desired

3.10- Timing and control unit:
Timing and control unit is a very important unit as it synchronizes the registers and
flow of data among system units. This unit consists of an oscillator and controller
sequencer which sends control signals needed for internal/external control of data
and other units.
The oscillator generates two-phase clock signals which aids in synchronizing all
the functional units of 8085 microprocessor.
Microprocessor Control Units: Phase 1: Fetch instruction from memory Phase 2: Execute
the instruction.
Memory Systems (RAM): Phase 1: Address setup (Put memory address on bus - Select
which memory cell to access) Phase 2: Data transfer (Read data from memory - Or write
data to memory)

5.B Instruction Cycle
The instructions in assembly language are termed as mnemonics. As we know,
microprocessor can only understand the machine language. So,
mnemonics  assembler  machine code.
An instruction is a command to the microprocessor to perform a given task on a
particular data (operand). Each instruction is of two parts.
1- Task to be performed, called the op-code and 2- The operand.
Operands (data to be worked on) can be specified in different ways. The instruction
may include an immediate operand or fetch the operand from an internal register or a
memory location. In some instructions, the operand is implicitly known.
Instruction Size: The 8085 instruction set is of three groups according to word
size:
One-byte instructions.
Two-byte instructions.
Three-byte instructions.
chunks.heading: 5.B Instruction Cycle

chunks.text:
5.B Instruction Cycle
One-byte instructions
A one-byte instruction includes both the op-code and a operand parts in the same
byte.
In the first instruction, operand registers C and A are specified in the instruction. In
the 2nd instruction, the operand is Reg. only B and the accumulator is not there.
Similarly, in the 3rd instruction, the accumulator A is assumed to be the implicit
operand.
These instructions are in 8-bit binary format in the memory and each requires one
memory location.
chunks.heading: 5.B Instruction Cycle

chunks.text:
5.B Instruction Cycle
Two-byte instructions
In a two-byte instruction, the first byte specifies the op-code and second byte specifies
the operand. If an 8-bit numeral is present in the instruction then the instruction will
be two-byte. Here, the numeral may be a data / address. For example: MVI A 35H &&
IN 29H.
Three-byte instructions
In a three-byte instruction, the first byte specifies the op-code, and the following two
bytes specify the 16-bit operand. Here, the numeral may be a data / address. For
example: LXI H 3500H && STA 2500H.

In the case of microprocessor, the operations are specified by using specific bit

In immediate addressing mode, operands are specified in the instruction itself. Examples
of immediate addressing mode
MVI A 05H  Move 05H in the accumulator.
ADI 06  Add 06H to the accumulator.
LXI H 2500H  Loads H:L pair with 2500H
When microprocessor executes the MVI B 45H, the processor fetches the 1st instruction
byte and determines that it must fetch one more byte from the next memory location.
Similarly, when microprocessor executes the LXI H 2500H, the processor fetches the 1st
instruction byte and determines that it must fetch two more bytes from the next two
memory locations.

chunks.text:
TIMING EFFECTS OF ADDRESSING MODES
The instructions having register or implicit addressing will be executing much
faster as compared to other addressing modes (those that need a memory
access). This is because both these addressing modes deal directly with the
processor’s hardware (the data already present in the hardware registers).
Also in these addressing modes, the instruction is always of one-byte and is
fetched in a single machine cycle.
As most of the time of the execution of an instruction is wasted in getting a data
from the memory or on how many machine cycles are required to execute such
instruction.
Also the number of machine cycles affected by the number of bytes required to
represent that instruction. Hence, as the number of bytes required representing
an instruction increases, then the execution time will increase.
Instruction Cycle

chunks.text:
TIMING EFFECTS OF ADDRESSING MODES
Examples of Timing of Timing Effect of Addressing Modes
A three-byte instruction requires more time for execution as compared to a two-
byte or a one-byte instruction.
So, we can say that the number of memory accesses required is the most
important factor in determining execution timing.
For example, the CALL instruction, which is a three-byte instruction requires five
machine cycles. In which three to access the complete instruction and two more
to push the contents of the PC onto the stack.
Now the same CALL operation can be performed by one-byte RSTn instruction.
This instruction will be executes in just three memory cycles.

instruction cycle : Time required to fetch, decode and execute an entire
instruction. It consists of:
Fetch cycle – The next instruction is fetched by the address stored in program counter
(PC) and then stored in the instruction register. Decode instruction – Decoder interprets the encoded instruction from instruction
register. Reading effective address – The address given in instruction is read from main memory
and required data is fetched. The effective address depends on direct addressing mode
or indirect addressing mode. Execution cycle – consists memory read (MR), memory write (MW), input output read
(IOR) and input output write (IOW)

memory or input/output devices is called machine cycle.

Programmable Peripheral Interface (PPI) 8255A
The 8255 is an IC used to simplify the interfacing of microprocessors with I/O
devices.
chunks.heading: Programmable Peripheral Interface (PPI) 8255A

chunks.text:
Data Bus Buffer
The tri-state bi-directional 8-bit buffer is used to interface the 8255A to the
microprocessor data bus (D0-D7).
Read write control logic
Manages all the internal and external transfers of both data and control word
register (CWR).
A0 and A1
These are the address lines of 8255A which are directly connected to the MP lower
address lines (A0 and A1). In conjunction with chip select, control the selection of one
of the three ports or the control word register in PPI.
Programmable Peripheral Interface (PPI) 8255A
chunks.heading: Data Bus Buffer

chunks.text:
RD and WR
A “LOW” on this pin enables 8255A to send data / status information to MP via data
bus (read operation) or enable MP to write data / control word register (CWR) value
to 8255 via data bus (write operation).
RESET
A “HIGH” on this pin clears the control word register (CWR) and all ports (A,B and C)
are set to input mode.
Group A and Group B controls
The function of each port is programmed by the system software. The MP “outputs” a
control word to the 8255 to set some information such as mode, bit-set/reset, that
initialize the configuration of 8255.
Each of control blocks (Group A and Group B) accept commands from read/write
control logic, receives “control words” from the internal data bus and issue the
proper commands to its associate ports.

Ports A, B and C
The 8255A contains three 8-bit ports (A, B and C). All can be configured in a
wide variety of functional characteristics by the system software. The major
function of each ports is 8-bit Input/output, and only Port C can be
configured as double 4-bit latch, it is used for control signal output and
status signal inputs in conjunction with ports A and B.
8255A Operational Description:
There are three basic I/O modes of operation that can be selected by the system
software after properly sets the control word register (CWR) format as per the
requirements.
Mode 0 – Basic Input/ Output
Mode 1 – Handshaking Input/ Output
Mode 2 – Bi-directional Bus.
In Mode 0 all ports (A, B and C) can be used as 8-bit I/O ports and configured by the
control word register (CWR).
Programmable Peripheral Interface (PPI) 8255A
chunks.heading: Ports A, B and C

chunks.text:
In Mode 1 only Port A and B configured as I/O while the upper 4-bit of port C
used as strobe signal  port A and lower 4-bit of port C used as strobe 
port B.
Mode 2 is available only for port A while port B can be used as simple I/O
mode and bit’s of port C used as strobe signal.
Except of these three modes of operation 8255A offers single Bit Set/ Reset
(BSR) features of port bits, which is limited to port C only.
All of these operations are maintained by a 8-bit CWR register .
Before using this PPI chip, user must initialize all of these 8-bit ports as input
or output with proper modes of operation according to the circuitry where it
will be placed.

A brief history of the ARM
The ARM came out of a company called Acorn Computers in United Kingdom
in the 1980s. Professor Steve of Manchester University worked define the
ARM architecture.
VLSI Technology Corp. produced the first ARM chip in 1985 for Acorn
Computers  Acorn RISC Machine (ARM). Unable to compete with x86 PCs,
the Acorn was forced to push the ARM chip into the single-chip
microcontroller market for embedded products.
Apple Corp. got interested in using the ARM chip for the PDA (personal digital
assistants) products. This renewed interest in the chip led to the creation of a
new company Advanced RISC Machine (ARM).
Apple had tried to sell a ARM-based PDA called Newton in the 1990s and it
was too early for its time.
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
ARM and Apple
This new company bet its entire fortune on selling rights to this new
chip to other silicon manufacturers. Since the early 1990s, an ever
increasing number of companies have licensed the right to make the
ARM chip.
ARM had lost the personal computer race that had started 20 years
earlier. The introduction of iPod in 2001 changed the fortune of that
company more than anything else.
The iPod used an enhanced version of ARM and became an instant
success. Since then Apple has been using the ARM chip in iPhone
and iPad. Today, the ARM microcontroller is the CPU of choice for
designing cell phone and other hand-held devices.

ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
In ARM, there are 13 general purpose registers  R0–R12.
The Special Function Registers in ARM
In ARM the R13, R14, R15, and CPSR (Current Program Status Register)
registers are called SFRs (special function registers) since each one is
dedicated to a specific function.
The function of each SFR is fixed by the CPU designer at the time of design
because it is used for control of the microcontroller or keeping track of
specific CPU status.
The R13 is set aside for stack pointer. The R14 is designated as link register
which holds the return address when the CPU calls a subroutine and the R15
is the program counter (PC) that points to the address of the next instruction
to be executed. The CPSR is used for keeping condition flags among other
things.
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
In contrast to SFRs, the GPRs (R0-R12) do not have any specific function and
are used for storing general data. For this reason, some ARM instruction
formats have only R0-R7 but every variation of ARM chip has R13-R15 SFRs.
Program Counter in the ARM
R15 is the program counter. As the CPU fetches the opcode from the program
memory, the program counter is incremented automatically to point to the next
instruction. The wider the program counter, the more memory locations a CPU can
access. That means a 32-bit program counter can access a maximum of 4G (232 = 4G)
bytes of program memory locations.

ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
The ARM has 4G bytes of directly accessible memory space. This memory space
has addresses 0 to 0xFFFFFFFF. The 4G bytes of memory space can be divided
into:
1. On-chip peripheral and I/O registers: This area is dedicated to general purpose I/O
(GPIO) - special function registers (SFRs) of peripherals such as timers, serial
communication, DMA, PIC, ADC. 2. On-chip data SRAM: A RAM space ranging from a #KB to #100s KBs is set aside mainly
for data storage (data variables - stack). 3. On-chip EEPROM: A memory block from 1KB to #KBs is set aside for EEPROM memory
is used for critical data. Not all ARM chips have on-chip EEPROM. 4. On-chip Flash ROM: A memory block from a #KB to #100s KBs is set aside for program
code. 5- Off-chip DRAM space: A DRAM memory ranging from #MBs to #100MBs can be
implemented for external memory connection.

A given ARM chip has the following address assignments. Calculate the space and the amount of memory given to each section. (a) Address range of 0x00100000 – 0x0010 0FFF for EEPROM
(b) Address range of 0x40000000 – 0x4000 7FFF for SRAM
(c) Address range of 0x00000000 – 0x0007 FFFF for Flash
(d) Address range of 0xFFFC 0000 – 0xFFFF FFFF for peripherals
(a) With EEPROM address space of 0x00100000 to 0010 0FFF, we have 00100FFF –
00100000 = 0FFF bytes. Converting 0FFF to decimal, we get 4,095 + 1, which equal 4KB. (b) With SRAM address space of 0x40000000 to 0x40007FFF, we have 40007FFF –
40000000 = 7FFF bytes. Converting to decimal, we get 32,767 + 1, which 32KB. (c) With Flash address space of 0000 to 7FFFF, we have 7FFFF bytes. Converting 7FFFF to
decimal, we get 524,287 + 1, which is equal to 512KB.

decimal, we get 524,287 + 1, which is equal to 512KB. (d) With SFR address space of FFFC0000 to FFFFFFFF, we have FFFFFFFF–FFFC0000 = 3FFFF
bytes. Converting 3FFFF to decimal, we get 262,143 + 1, which is equal to 256KB.

ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
CPUs use registers to store data temporarily. To program in
Assembly language, we need to understand the architecture of a
given CPU and the role registers play in processing data.
GPR vs. SPR
General Purpose Registers in the ARM
ARM microcontrollers have many registers for arithmetic and logic
operations. In a CPU, registers are used to store information temporarily (data
to be processed / address pointing to the data to be fetched). All of ARM
registers are 32-bit wide.
With a 32-bit data type, any data larger than 32 bits must be broken into 32-
bit chunks before it is processed. The 32-bit data size of the ARM is often
referred as word.
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
This is in contrast to x86 CPU in which word is defined as 16-bit.
In ARM the 16-bit data is referred to as half-word. Therefore ARM
supports byte, half-word (two byte), and word (four bytes) data
types.

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
ARM Instruction Format
The ARM CPU uses the tri-part instruction format for most instructions. One of
the most common format is:
instruction destination,source1,source2
Depending on the instruction, the source2 can be a register, immediate value,
or memory.
MOV instruction
Simply stated, the MOV instruction copies immediate data into register or
from register to register. It has the following formats:
MOV Rn,Op2 ;load Rn register with Op2 contents.
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Op2 can be an immediate (constant) number #K which is an 8-bit value that
can be 0–255 in decimal, (00–FF in hex). Op2 can also be a register Rm.
The following instruction loads the R2 register with a value of 0x25 (25 in hex).
MOV R2,#0x25 ;load R2 with immediate value 0x25 (R2 = 0x25)
The following instruction loads the R1 register with the value 0x87 (87 in hex).
MOV R1,#0x87 ;Copy immediate value 0x87 into R1 (R1 = 0x87)
The following instruction loads R5 with the value of R7
MOV R5, R7 ;Copy contents of R7 into R5 (R5 = R7)
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
MOV R1,#50 , R1 is loaded with 50 in decimal, whereas in
MOV R1,#0x50 , R1 is loaded with 50 in hex ( 80 in decimal).
If values 0 to FF are moved into a 32-bit register, the rest of the bits are
assumed to be all zeros.
For example, in “MOV R1,#0x5” the result will be R1=0x00000005; that
is, R1 = 00000000000000000000000000000101 in binary.
We cannot load immediate values larger than 0xFF (255) into registers R0 
R12 using the MOV instruction.
For example, the following instruction is not valid:
MOV R5,#0x999999 ;invalid instruction. The reason is the fact that although
the ARM instruction is 32-bit wide, only 8-bits of MOV instruction can be
used as an immediate value which can take values not larger than 0xFF (255).

ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Load Store instructions
The ARM allows direct access to all locations in the memory. Every
instruction of ARM is fixed at 32-bit (fixed size instruction is one of the most
important characteristics of RISC architecture). In cases where there is no
need for all the 32-bit, the ARM has added zero to make the instruction
fixed at 32-bit. LDR Rd,[Rx] ;load Rd with the contents of location pointed to by Rx register. Rx is an address between 0x00000000 to 0xFFFFFFFF
The LDR instruction tells the CPU to load one word (32-bit or 4-bytes) from a base
address pointed to by Rx into the GPR Rd. The locations can be in the SRAM / Flash
memory. That means the Rx register gives the base address of the memory in which it holds
the data.

the data. Therefore if R5=0x80000, the CPU will fetch into register R2, the contents

After this instruction is executed, it must be noted that the unused portion (the

Executing the LDRB Instruction
There are situations that we do not need to bring 4 bytes of data into GPR. An UART is such a
case. The UART registers are generally 8-bit and take only one memory space location (memory
mapped I/O). Using LDRB, we can bring into GPR a single byte of data from UART registers. This
is a widely used instruction for accessing the 8-bit I/O and peripheral ports.

Using instruction BNE for looping
The BNE (branch if not equal) instruction uses the zero-flag in the
CPSR status register.
BACK ……… ;start of the loop
……… ;body of the loop
……… ;body of the loop
SUBS Rn,Rn,#1 ;Rn = Rn - 1, set the flag Z = 1 if Rn = 0
BNE BACK ;branch if Z = 0
In the last two instructions, the Rn is decremented; if it is not zero, it branches
(jumps) back to the target address referred to by the label. Prior to the start of the
loop, the Rn is loaded with the counter value for the number of repetitions. Notice

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
C, the carry flag
This flag is set whenever there is a carry out from the D31 bit. This flag bit is
affected after a 32-bit addition or subtraction. Z, the zero flag
The zero flag reflects the result of an arithmetic or logic operation. If the result
is zero, then Z = 1. N, the negative flag
The negative flag reflects the result of an arithmetic operation. If the D31 bit of
the result is zero, then N = 0 and the result is positive. If the D31 bit is one,
then N = 1 and the result is negative. The negative and V flag bits are used for
the signed number arithmetic operations. V, the overflow flag
This flag is set whenever the result of a signed number operation is too large,
causing the high-order bit to overflow into the sign bit.
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
he result of a signed number operation is too large,
causing the high-order bit to overflow into the sign bit. In general, the carry flag is used to detect errors in unsigned arithmetic
operations while the overflow flag is used to detect errors in signed arithmetic
operations.

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
If we need an instruction to update the value of status bits in
CPSR, we have to put S suffix at the end of instructions. That
means, for example, ADDS instead of ADD is used.
T Flag (Thumb state)
T = 1 → Processor is executing Thumb instructions (16-bit compressed instructions)
T = 0 → Processor is executing ARM instructions (32-bit instructions)
Purpose: Allows switching between ARM and Thumb instruction sets for better code density
I Flag (IRQ interrupt)
I = 1 → Disables IRQ interrupts
I = 0 → Enables IRQ interrupts
Purpose: Controls whether the processor can respond to standard hardware interrupts
F Flag (FIQ interrupt)
F = 1 → Disables FIQ (Fast Interrupt Requests)
F = 0 → Enables FIQ interrupts
Purpose: Controls the higher-priority, faster-response interrupts

ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Show the status of the Z flag during the execution of the following
program:
Solution:
The Z flag is raised when the result is zero. Otherwise, it is cleared (zero). Thus:
MOV R2,#4 ;R2 = 4
MOV R3,#2 ;R3 = 2
MOV R4,#4 ;R4 = 4
SUBS R5,R2,R3 ;R5 = R2 - R3 (R5 = 4 - 2 = 2)
MOV R2,#4 ;R2 = 4
MOV R3,#2 ;R3 = 2
MOV R4,#4 ;R4 = 4
SUBS R5,R2,R4 ;R5 = R2 - R4 (R5 = 4 - 4 = 0)

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Some instructions affect all the four flag bits C, Z, V, N (e.g., ADDS).
Some instructions affect no flag bits at all such as branch
instructions. Some instructions affect only some of the flag bits. The
logic instructions (e.g., ANDS) are in this category.
Flag bits and decision making
There are instructions that
will make a conditional jump
(branch) based on the status
of flag bits.
ARM Branch (Jump) Instructions Using Flag Bits

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
ARM data type
ARM has four data types. They are bit, byte (8-bit), half-word (16-bit) and word (32-bit). Data format representation
There are several ways to represent a byte of data in the ARM assembler. The numbers can
be in hex, binary, decimal, or ASCII formats. 1-Hex numbers
To represent Hex numbers in an ARM assembler we put 0x (0X) in front of the
number like this: MOV R1,#0x99
2-Decimal numbers
To indicate decimal numbers in some ARM assemblers such as Keil we simply use
the decimal (12). MOV R7,#12
3-Binary numbers
To represent binary numbers in an ARM assembler we put 2_ in front of the
number.
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
MOV R7,#12
3-Binary numbers
To represent binary numbers in an ARM assembler we put 2_ in front of the
number. It is as follows: MOV R6,#2_10011001
4-ASCII characters
To represent ASCII data in an ARM assembler we use single quotes as follows: MOV
R3,#‘2’ ;R3 = 00110010 or 32 in hex
To represent a string, double quotes are used; and for defining ASCII strings, we use
the DCB directive.

ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Assembler directives
While instruction Mnemonics (Op-codes) tell the CPU what to do,
directives (pseudo instructions) give directions to the assembler. For
example, the MOV and ADD instructions are commands to the CPU,
but EQU, END, and ENTRY are directives to the assembler.
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

While instructions tell the CPU what to do, directives (also called pseudo instructions) give
directions to the assembler. For example, the MOV and ADD instructions are commands to
the CPU, but EQU, END, and ENTRY are directives to the assembler.

ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
DCB directive (define constant byte)
The DCB directive allocates a byte size memory and initializes the values.

DCW directive (define constant half-word)
The DCW directive allocates a half-word size memory and initializes the values.
MYDATA DCW 0x20, 0xF230, 5000, 0x9CD7
DCD directive (define constant word)
The DCD directive allocates a word size memory and initializes the values.
MYDATA DCD 0x200000, 0xF30F5, 5000000, 0xFFFF9CD7

program memory using the directives. It shows how the data is stored in memory.

allocated for each data.
The DCD allocates 4-bytes for each data. As a result the lowest byte of

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Assembly Instruction Format
An Assembly language instruction consists of four fields:
[label] mnemonic [operands] [;comment]
Brackets indicate that a field is optional and not all lines have them.
MOV R3,#0x55
MOV R2,#0x67
ADD R2,R2,R3 ;R2 = R2 + R3
ADD and MOV are the mnemonics that produce opcodes; the “0x55”
and “0x67” are the operands.
Remember directives (END && ENTRY) do not generate any machine
code and are used only by the assembler, as opposed to instructions
that are translated into machine code (opcode) for CPU to execute.
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Assembly Instruction Format
AREA PROG_Lec11, CODE, READONLY
ENTRY
MOV R1, #0x25 ;R1 = 0x25
MOV R2, #0x34 ;R2 = 0x34
ADD R3, R2,R1 ;R3 = R2 + R1
HERE B HERE
END
Notice the label “HERE” in the label field in the above code. In the B
(Branch) statement the ARM is told to stay in this loop indefinitely.

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
ARM Addressing Modes
The CPU can access operands (data) in various ways, called
addressing modes. The number of addressing modes is determined
when the microprocessor is designed and cannot be changed.
Immediate addressing mode
In the immediate addressing mode, the source operand is a constant. In
immediate addressing mode, as the name implies, when the instruction is
assembled, the opcode comes immediately after the opcode.
MOV R9,#0x25 ;move the hexadecimal value 0x25 into R9
MOV R3,#62 ;load the decimal value 62 into R3
ADD R6,#0x40 ;add the hexadecimal value 0x40 to R6
Immediate Addressing Mode
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
ARM Addressing Modes
Register addressing mode
The register addressing mode involves the use of registers to hold the data to be
manipulated.
MOV R6,R2 ;copy the contents of R2 into R6
ADD R1,R1,R3 ;add the contents of R3 to contents of R1
SUB R7,R7,R2 ;subtract R2 from R7
Register Addressing Mode
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
ARM Addressing Modes
Register Indirect Addressing Mode (Indexed addressing mode)
In the register indirect addressing mode, the address of the memory
location where the operand resides is held by a register.
STR R5,[R6] ;move R5 into the memory location pointed to by R6
LDR R10,[R3] ;move into R10 the contents of the memory location pointed to by R3.
Register Indirect Addressing Mode

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Looping and Branch Instructions
In this section we first discuss how to perform a looping action in
ARM and then the branch (jump) instructions, both conditional and
unconditional.
MOV R0,#0 ;R0 = 0
MOV R1,#9 ;R1 = 9
ADD R0,R0,R1 ;R0 = R0 + R1, add 9 to R0 (Now R0 is 0x09)
ADD R0,R0,R1 ;R0 = R0 + R1, add 9 to R0 (Now R0 is 0x12)
ADD R0,R0,R1 ;R0 = R0 + R1, add 9 to R0 (Now R0 is 0x1B)
ADD R0,R0,R1 ;R0 = R0 + R1, add 9 to R0 (Now R0 is 0x24)
ADD R0,R0,R1 ;R0 = 0x2D
ADD R0,R0,R1 ;R0 = 0x36
In the above program, we add 0x9 to R0 six-times. That makes 6 × 9 = 54 = 0x36.
One problem with the above program is that too much code space would be
needed to increase the number of repetitions to 50 or 1000.
chunks.heading: ARM Architecture - Assembly Language

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Using instruction BNE for looping
The BNE (branch if not equal) instruction uses the zero-flag in the
CPSR status register.
BACK ……… ;start of the loop
……… ;body of the loop
……… ;body of the loop
SUBS Rn,Rn,#1 ;Rn = Rn - 1, set the flag Z = 1 if Rn = 0
BNE BACK ;branch if Z = 0
In the last two instructions, the Rn is decremented; if it is not zero, it branches
(jumps) back to the target address referred to by the label. Prior to the start of the
loop, the Rn is loaded with the counter value for the number of repetitions. Notice
that the BNE instruction refers to the Z-flag of the status register affected by the
previous instruction, SUBS.
Rn = ???

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Example
Write a program to (a) clear R0, (b) add 9 to R0 a thousand times,
then (c) place the sum in R4.
;– this program adds value 9 to the R0 a 1000 times –
AREA EXAMPLE1, CODE, READONLY
ENTRY
LDR R2,=1000 ;R2 = 1000 (decimal) for counter (more than 255)
MOV R0,#0 ;R0 = 0 (sum)
AGAIN ADD R0,R0,#9 ;R0 = R0 + 9 (add 09 to R1, R1 = sum)
SUB R2,R2,#1 ;R2 = R2 - 1 and set the flags. Decrement counter
BNE AGAIN ;repeat until COUNT = 0 (when Z = 1)
MOV R4,R0 ;store the sum in R4
HERE B HERE ;stay here
END
!

chunks.text:
ARM Architecture - Assembly Language
Example
It must be emphasized again that we must use SUBS instead of SUB since the SUB
instruction will not update the flags. Since we are monitoring the Z-flag for the
loop counter we must use SUBS instruction for the decrementing the counter.
;– this program adds value 9 to the R0 a 1000 times –
AREA EXAMPLE1, CODE, READONLY
ENTRY
LDR R2,=1000 ;R2 = 1000 (decimal) for counter
MOV R0,#0 ;R0 = 0 (sum)
AGAIN ADD R0,R0,#9 ;R0 = R0 + 9 (add 09 to R1, R1 = sum)
SUBS R2,R2,#1 ;R2 = R2 - 1 and set the flags. Decrement counter
BNE AGAIN ;repeat until COUNT = 0 (when Z = 1)
MOV R4,R0 ;store the sum in R4
HERE B HERE ;stay here
END

chunks.text:
8259 PIC
Programmable Interrupt Controller
Features:
Can manage 8-interrupts at a time based on the setting of control registers
ICW1-4 and OCW1-3.
Handles many interrupt requests simultaneously based on their types and
priority.
Can vector the interrupt requests anywhere in memory, but the CALL address
has to be spaced in an interval of 4/8.
Can accept either edge-triggered (default) or level-triggered interrupt
requests.
Compatible with both 8-bit (8085) as well as 16-bit (8086) microprocessors.
Can mask each interrupt request individually from within IMR.
Can read the status of pending, masked, and in-service interrupts.
Can be extended to accept more than 8-level interrupts by
cascading slave 8259s.

indicate that the request is accepted. Then, the op-code for the CALL instruction is placed on the data bus. When the
processor decodes the CALL instruction, it places 2 more INTA signal on the data bus. When the 8259 receives the 2nd INTA, it places the low-order byte of the CALL
address on the data bus. At the 3rd INTA, it places the high-order byte on the data bus.

Programmable Interrupt Controller
To implement interrupts, the Interrupt Enable flip-flop in the
8085 should be enabled, and the 8259 requires two types of
control words:
- Initialization Command Words (ICW)
- Operational Command Words (OCW)
The 8259 can be initialized with 4-ICWs; the first two are
essential, and the other two are optional based on the modes
being used (they mainly controls Master/Slave modes).
Once initialized, the 8259 can be set up to operate in various
modes by using three different OCWs.

Serial vs. Parallel Communication
RS-232 is a standard for how that hardware
sends and receives signals.
Data skew refers to the timing mismatch between parallel data
signals transmitted over multiple channels.
Crosstalk is unwanted coupling of signals between adjacent
communication channels (wires, traces), causing interference
that corrupts the transmitted data.

qa_pairs.question: What is MSA University and where is it located?
qa_pairs.answer: October University for Modern Sciences and Arts (MSA University) is a leading private university located in 6th of October City, Giza, Egypt, at the intersection of the 26th of July Mehwar Road and Wahat Road, about 30 km from central Cairo. The official hotline is 16672 (international landline 002 0216672), support email is info@msa.edu.eg, and the website is msa.edu.eg.
qa_pairs.topic: MSA University Overview and Location

qa_pairs.question: What should students know about Dual British Degree Partnerships in MSA University Overview & Faculties?
qa_pairs.answer: Q: Which British universities partner with MSA University for dual degrees? A: MSA University operates a dual degree system where graduates earn both an Egyptian bachelor degree accredited by the Supreme Council of Universities and a British bachelor degree validated by either the University of Greenwich or the University of Bedfordshire, enabling direct postgraduate study in the UK without traditional degree equivalence. Q: Which MSA faculties are partnered with the University of Greenwich? A: Six faculties partner with the University of Greenwich: Faculty of Engineering, Faculty of Pharmacy, Faculty of Computer Sciences, Faculty of Biotechnology, Faculty of Management Sciences, and Faculty of Nutrition and Food Technology.
qa_pairs.topic: Dual British Degree Partnerships

qa_pairs.question: Does MSA University provide campus buses and where do I subscribe?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes. MSA University operates a private bus fleet covering Greater Cairo and Giza including 6th of October, Sheikh Zayed, Palm Hills, Dream Park, Al Motamayez, Hadayek El Ahram, Haram, Faisal, Mohandessin, Maadi, Mokattam, Nasr City, Heliopolis, Shubra, New Cairo, Al Rehab, Madinaty, and Helwan. Students manage bus subscriptions at the official Bus Room in Room K108.
qa_pairs.topic: University Transportation and Bus Services

qa_pairs.question: What is the attendance rule and absence limit at MSA University?
qa_pairs.answer: Students at MSA University must maintain a minimum attendance rate of 75 percent across all lectures, tutorials, and laboratories for each module. Falling below 75 percent attendance (even with medical or emergency absences) leads to deprivation from the final exam and automatic failure in that module. For regular classes, late entry is permitted only during the first 5 minutes; after 5 minutes the student is marked absent.
qa_pairs.topic: MSA University Attendance and Class Arrival Rules

qa_pairs.question: What should students know about Exam Entry Rules and Academic Integrity in MSA Academic Rules & Admission Bylaws?
qa_pairs.answer: Q: What are the late arrival rules for midterm and final exams at MSA University? A: For 1.5 hour midterm exams, students are allowed entry only within the first 15 minutes. For 3 hour final exams, entry is permitted up to the first 30 minutes. Students must bring their official MSA University Student ID card to attend examinations and enter campus facilities. Q: What are the plagiarism and academic misconduct rules at MSA University? A: MSA University enforces strict academic integrity rules. Plagiarism includes quoting words or paragraphs without proper citation, paraphrasing someone else's ideas without acknowledgment, borrowing unacknowledged data, or copying another student's assignments, computer code, or exam answers.
qa_pairs.topic: Exam Entry Rules and Academic Integrity

qa_pairs.question: How do credit hours, GPA, and academic probation work at MSA University?
qa_pairs.answer: MSA University follows a 4.0 letter grading scale (A through D, Fail = 0). Bachelor programs typically require at least 140 credit hours across four academic years (8 semesters), depending on the faculty. In the summer semester, students may register for a maximum of 7 credit hours. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 is required for good academic standing and graduation. Students whose cumulative GPA falls below 2.0 are placed on academic probation with restricted course load until their cumulative GPA returns to 2.0 or higher. When repeating a module, only the highest earned grade counts toward the cumulative GPA.
qa_pairs.topic: Credit Hours, GPA Scale, and Academic Probation

qa_pairs.question: What is required for course registration and the English Language Placement Test (ELPT) at MSA University?
qa_pairs.answer: Before registering courses during the academic calendar advising period, students must register their bank tuition payment receipts with the MSA Accounting Department. All new applicants must take the English Language Placement Test (ELPT) unless exempt with valid IELTS, TOEFL, IGCSE English grade B or 6+, IB, Canadian diploma, or qualifying SAT, ACT, or EST scores. The online ELPT can be taken one time only; any retake or reset must be taken physically on campus.
qa_pairs.topic: Registration, Financial Clearance, and English Placement Test (ELPT)

qa_pairs.question: What should students know about Admission Requirements and Required Documents at MSA University in MSA Academic Rules & Admission Bylaws?
qa_pairs.answer: Q: What general documents are required for admission to MSA University? A: All new applicants submit 5 recent passport photos, 2 original computerized Egyptian birth certificates (or authenticated birth certificates for non Egyptians), copies of student and parent National ID cards, passport copy if available, and for Egyptian male students military service Form 2 Gond plus Form 6 or 7 Gond. Q: What are the certificate requirements for Thanaweya Amma, IGCSE, and American Diploma at MSA University? A: Thanaweya Amma students submit their original stamped certificate matching the required faculty section (Scientific Math for Engineering; Scientific Science for Pharmacy, Dentistry, and Physical Therapy).

qa_pairs.answer: **خطوات التقديم والالتحاق بجامعة MSA** 1. **Step 1 — Submit Online Application:** Fill out the online application form on the MSA Admissions portal. 2. **Step 2 — Check Email for Application Payment Details:** Follow the emailed payment instructions. 3. **Step 3 — ELPT Exam & Profiling Questionnaire:** Sit for the English Language Placement Test (if not exempt) and complete the profiling questionnaire. 4. **Step 4 — Personal Interview & Parents' Involvement Session:** Receive an email to schedule the student's faculty interview/club activity and mandatory in-person Parents' Involvement Program session. 5. **Step 5 — Conditional Offer Letter:** Check email for the official conditional offer letter and payment order to complete tuition payment on campus. 6.

qa_pairs.question: What should students know about 4. Admission for Transfer Students (التحويل من جامعات أخرى) in MSA Official Admission Guide, Min Scores, ELPT & Documents?
qa_pairs.answer:
- **CRITICAL RULE:** Transfer students **MUST NOT withdraw** their file from their current university until they receive explicit final approval and acceptance from an official MSA Admission Officer. - **Minimum GPA Required:**
- **Faculty of Dentistry:** Minimum cumulative GPA of **3.0 to 3.5**. - **All other MSA faculties:** Minimum cumulative GPA of **2.0**. - **Required Transfer Documents & Steps:**
- Full copy of high school documents (to verify eligibility). - Good Conduct letter (خطاب حسن سير وسلوك) from previous university. - Military service forms for Egyptian males (`Namouzag 2 + 6 Gond`). - Copy of National ID card (and passport for non-Egyptians).

qa_pairs.answer:
- All international (non-Egyptian) students must apply through the **Study in Egypt (إدرس في مصر)** platform in 3 steps:
1. Create an account and upload final original stamped high school certificates. 2. Receive the official **Nomination Letter** after certificate review and score calculation. 3. Submit original stamped documents to MSA University and pay tuition fees in USD on campus at NBE. - **MSA Key Facts & UK Partners:**
- Founded in 1996, 32,000+ graduates, 36 student clubs, 11 faculties, dual Egyptian + UK degrees. - **University of Greenwich (UK) validates 6 faculties:** Engineering, Pharmacy, Computer Science, Biotechnology, Management Sciences, Nutrition & Food Technology.

qa_pairs.question: What is the architectural design and campus layout of MSA University in 6th of October?
qa_pairs.answer: MSA University occupies a 50 acre permanent campus in 6th of October City designed around open green landscapes, pedestrian courtyards, natural ventilation, and eco friendly sustainable architecture. Campus architectural highlights include the MSA Center of Earth constructed with Compressed Stabilized Earth Blocks (CSEB), the landmark 1,150 seat Opera House in Building G, the El Degwi Mosque, 31 cafeterias and food courts, and comprehensive sports grounds including football, basketball, volleyball, padel courts, and the MSA Gym.
qa_pairs.topic: MSA University Campus Layout and Architectural Design

qa_pairs.question: What should students know about MSA University Buildings Directory (Buildings 1 to 13, SSB, and Building G) in MSA Campus Buildings & Architecture?
qa_pairs.answer: Q: What is located in Building 1, Building 2 (SSB), and Building 3 at MSA University? A: Building 1 houses University Administration, the Faculty of Languages, the Faculty of Mass Communication, and the Faculty of Management Sciences. Building 2 is the Student Services Building (SSB), serving as the central hub for student affairs, student activities, career events like Build Your Future, seminar spaces, and the renovated campus Cinema Hall. Building 3 houses the major scientific and technical faculties: Faculty of Pharmacy, Faculty of Engineering, Faculty of Biotechnology, Faculty of Computer Science, and Faculty of Dentistry. Q: What is located in Building 4, Building 5, Building 6, and Building 7 at MSA University?
qa_pairs.topic: MSA University Buildings Directory (Buildings 1 to 13, SSB, and Building G)

qa_pairs.question: What does the Architecture Department at MSA University study and what facilities does it have?
qa_pairs.answer: The Faculty of Engineering offers a Bachelor degree in Architectural Systems Engineering (ASE) validated with the University of Greenwich. Its studio based curriculum covers Architectural Design, History and Theories of Architecture, Urban Planning, Landscape Design, Interior Design, Environmental Control Systems, Computer Graphics, and Construction Management. Students work in dedicated architectural design studios, digital computer labs, engineering workshops in Building 6, and sustainable architecture spaces such as the MSA Center of Earth.
qa_pairs.topic: Architectural Systems Engineering (ASE) Department at MSA University

qa_pairs.question: How do room numbers and building letters work at MSA University?
qa_pairs.answer: MSA University room codes combine a building letter and a three digit number where the first digit indicates the floor and the last two digits indicate the room number: 1xx is the First floor at ground level (no stairs or elevator needed), 2xx is the Second floor upstairs, 3xx is the Third floor, and 4xx is the Fourth floor. For example, Room C111 is in Building C on the ground level First floor (Room 11), and Room G204 is in Building G on the Second floor (Room 04).
qa_pairs.topic: MSA University Room Numbering System and Building Map

qa_pairs.question: What should students know about Complete MSA Building Letters and Numbered Blocks in MSA Rooms & Building Locator Guide?
qa_pairs.answer: Q: What is the mapping between MSA lettered buildings (A, B, C, D, E, G, H, K, M, SSB) and numbered buildings (1 to 13)? A: Building A (Building 1) houses University Administration, Faculty of Languages, Faculty of Mass Communication, and Faculty of Management Sciences. Building B (Building 2 / SSB) is the Student Services Building housing Student Affairs, registration, student activities, seminar rooms, and the campus Cinema Hall. Building C (Building 3) houses the Faculty of Pharmacy, Faculty of Engineering, Faculty of Biotechnology, Faculty of Computer Science, and Faculty of Dentistry. Building D (Building 4) houses specialized scientific laboratories and Dentistry Outpatient Clinics.
qa_pairs.topic: Complete MSA Building Letters and Numbered Blocks

qa_pairs.question: Where is Room K108, the Bus Room, the Library, the Gym, the Opera House, Student Affairs (SSB), and the Dental Clinics?
qa_pairs.answer: Room K108 (Building K, First floor) is the official MSA Bus Subscription Room. The Main University Library and MSA Gym are in Building 7. The 1,150 seat Opera House is in Building G. Student Affairs, registration services, and the campus Cinema Hall are in Building 2 (Building B / SSB — Student Services Building). Dentistry Outpatient Clinics and scientific labs are in Building 4 (Building D), Building H (Research Center), and Building 11 (Dentistry Extension). Engineering workshops are in Building 6.

qa_pairs.question: ما هي المعلومات الأساسية حول نظام ترقيم القاعات والغرف ودليل المباني في جامعة MSA في MSA Rooms & Building Locator Guide؟
qa_pairs.answer: س: إزاي أعرف مكان القاعة أو الغرفة في جامعة MSA من رقمها؟ ج: يعتمد ترقيم القاعات في جامعة MSA على حرف المبنى متبوعاً بثلاثة أرقام، حيث يدل الرقم الأول على الدور والرقمان الأخيران على رقم الغرفة: 0xx تعني الدور الأرضي، و1xx تعني الدور الأول، و2xx تعني الدور الثاني، و3xx تعني الدور الثالث، و4xx تعني الدور الرابع. مثلاً غرفة K108 موجودة في مبنى K الدور الأول غرفة 08 (مكتب اشتراكات الأتوبيسات)، وقاعة G204 في مبنى G الدور الثاني غرفة 04. س: فين مكان المكتبة، الجيم، شؤون الطلاب، الأوبرا، مكتب الأتوبيس، الكليات، وعيادات الأسنان في MSA؟ ج: شؤون الطلاب والأنشطة والسينما في مبنى 2 (مبنى B / SSB). الإدارة واللغات والإعلام والإدارة في مبنى 1 (مبنى A). الهندسة والحاسبات والصيدلة والتكنولوجيا الحيوية وطب الأسنان في مبنى 3 (مبنى C).

qa_pairs.question: What should students know about Top 5 Frequently Asked Questions About MSA University (Online FAQ Dataset) in MSA Top 5 Internet FAQs (Bilingual)?
qa_pairs.answer: Q: How does the MSA British Dual Degree work and is equivalency needed in the UK? A: Upon graduation from MSA University, students receive two accredited bachelor degrees: one approved by the Egyptian Ministry of Higher Education and Supreme Council of Universities, and a second validated by a UK partner university (University of Greenwich for Engineering, Computer Science, Pharmacy, Biotechnology, Management Sciences, and Nutrition; University of Bedfordshire for Mass Communication, Languages, Arts and Design, and Physical Therapy). Graduates can pursue postgraduate studies in the UK and internationally without traditional degree equivalency procedures. Q: Are MSA University graduates eligible to join Egyptian Professional Syndicates? A: Yes.
